lens: design concept, art direction, hierarchy and restraint vs ref-02

margins_css_px.verdict: FAIL: bottom is 9.3 px (2.5 mm) off the declared 64 px margin, over the 1 mm tolerance

column_end_heights.verdict: FAIL: fix_dead_space, the columns end at visibly different heights

measurements.left_edges: item names x=64 (col1) and x=430 (col2), 0 px deviation: pass
measurements.header_spacing: section head to sub head 31 px in every case, section gap 52 px (4U) in every case, section tops aligned at y=376 in both columns: pass
measurements.baseline_grid: no shared grid. Item boxes are 38.2 or 55.4 px (not multiples of 13), so rows do not register across columns (Manhattan 494.7 vs Anejo 477.5; Daiquiri 565.3 vs Cognac 548.0)
measurements.hierarchy_ratio: section heads 18 px vs item names 17.5 px = 1.03:1. The level is carried only by caps, tracking and colour

price_eye_travel.verdict: inline prices, 1 em hop on every row: pass. The phone 57.9% is the name's own length

measurements.price_format: integers, no $, tabular figures, weight 400 in ink-2 on every row: consistent
measurements.dead_space: the text in each 322 px column fills only about 50-60% of its width, so a band about 130-180 px wide runs empty down the right side of both columns. Together with the 55 px uneven column foot, this is empty canvas with no job
measurements.bleed: the plough line runs 24 px (6.4 mm) past the right trim; the sun runs about 34 px past the right trim and about 100 px past the top trim: pass

top_problem: The thesis (a contour plough line whose headlands are grecas, with the sun setting behind Iowa land) is clever on paper, but the render reads as a generic 1970s retro sunset with racing stripes. The three rounded-looking hairpins do not read as a step-fret or as ploughed furrows, so the gesture passes the substitution test only in the proposal text, not on the page. The boldest missing idea: make the furrow line the menu's actual structure. Let the ploughed field run down the page and carry the sections, with the furrow pitch becoming the row grid, instead of a band of stripes parked between the masthead and a plain two-column list. Beside ref-02 panel 2, which layers stair, agave, sun and texture into one worked composition, this is sparse rather than restrained: flat digital fills, no materiality, and a reading layer that is a default list.
remove: The cream knock-out of the wordmark inside the sun. It cuts the T mid-arm, so the word reads as 'CANT' + 'INA' (an unfortunate English word), and it adds a second trick on top of the sun. Either drop it, or move the sun so its edge falls cleanly in the gap between T and I.
fixes: Close the measured failures under criterion 6: bring the bottom margin to 64 px (it is now 73.3) and balance the column feet to within 1 mm (now 54.8 px apart), for example by snapping the section gaps to the grid or moving Cider so both columns end on the same baseline.

Make the gesture legible as its thesis: turn the headlands into true squared greca hooks (an inward return), and add enough furrows at a tight pitch that the band reads as a ploughed field rather than three paperclip stripes. Ideally carry the furrows under or between the columns so the land becomes the page's row structure.
Set a real 13 px baseline grid: make item boxes 39 and 52/65 px (multiples of U) so rows in the two columns register, and fix the sub-head-to-item gap at a grid value (now 7.8 px).

Strengthen the hierarchy: section heads at 18 px against 17.5 px names are one level only in colour. Take the heads to about 24 to 26 px, or set them in Chango at small size, so the head level reads at a glance in dim light.

Fix the dead right half of each column: narrow the column measure to about 240 px and reinvest the space in an asymmetric grid, a wider gutter or the land art, or run the cocktail descriptions to a wider measure. Empty canvas is not whitespace.

lens: items and prices against draft_doc.json; ingredient names and description completeness (public_components respected); section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The cocktail descriptions are complete, but the other 10 of the 14 items only repeat or restate their names, with no missing_ingredients flag. The beers have no ABV (and 'Crisp pale lager' does not name a style for the Czech Pilsner), the wines have no region (Brut Rosé has no grape either), and the spirits have no brand or age statement ('Blanco tequila pour', 'VSOP Cognac pour'). Criterion 8 counts missing ingredients with no flag as an automatic fail, so it scores 40 or below.
problems: All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Dry Cider 8. No item is invented or dropped, and no tagline states an item fact.
public_components is respected: aromatic bitters is correctly left off the Manhattan. The Old Fashioned's bitters are public, so printing them is correct.

The four garnishes (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry) are not in draft_doc.json. The designer admits they were not re-queried this round and cites only the Coordinator's brief. The gate passes on the assumption that phg.recipe_versions confirms them; the accuracy reviewer must verify them, and if any one does not match, content_integrity fails.

The description style is inconsistent. Three cocktails are lowercase middot lists with no full stop. The Margarita alone adds a full sentence ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). The non-cocktail lines are fragments that read like taxonomy labels ('Dry red wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA').
The Czech Pilsner's style is only implied by its name, and 'Crisp pale lager' adds nothing. None of the three draft beers has an ABV, and nothing asks for it.

The flow splits related categories. Cider sits at the foot of column 2, separated from Beer in column 1. Spirits sit before Wine, although the scorecard order is cocktails, beer, wine, spirits. Agave-first can be justified for this venue but the proposal does not argue it. Margarita was moved ahead of Manhattan with a reason but no note to the client.

The columns are unbalanced. Column 1 ends about 110 px above column 2, and column 2's short names leave the right third of the page empty for the whole reading layer. The large gaps between sections look like leftover space, not pacing, and the gap between the plough line and the content is large.
The draft's title ('Bar menu') and subtitle were replaced by the wordmark 'CANTINA', which is not in the draft, and no open point notes this. It reads as a venue name that no source provides.
'Cognac VSOP 18' still reads a little like an age or proof figure, even with the lighter price weight.
fixes: Add a missing_ingredients request to proposal.md and the handoff for beer ABV (and a confirmed style for all three beers), wine region (and a grape for the Brut Rosé), and spirit brand or age, and show a visible placeholder or ask the client instead of shipping descriptions that repeat the names.

Set every description in one pattern: middot ingredient lists for cocktails, style · ABV for beer, grape · region for wine, and type · age for spirits. Either give every cocktail a sourced tasting sentence or give none of them one.

Move Cider directly under Beer, or retitle the column 'Beer & Cider'. Either put Wine before Spirits or state the agave-first reason in the proposal, and balance the column ends to within one item height.
Confirm the four garnishes against phg.recipe_versions.garnish before filing, and remove any garnish that does not match exactly.
Replace 'CANTINA' with the draft title or a venue name the client has confirmed, or list it as an open point that needs sign-off, so the menu does not state an unsourced name.

lens: Ingredient, garnish and label tracing to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 215); how descriptions and prices sit together and the price-to-item gate in preview-letter.png
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source. All four garnishes the designer did not check match phg.recipe_versions: Margarita f06abb74 'Lime wheel', Manhattan 9fb77eaa 'Cocktail cherry', House Daiquiri 14d45e57 'Lime coin', Brown Butter Old Fashioned 7095fd3d 'Orange peel'. All 14 prices match menu_items.menu_price. The weak point is the descriptions: 10 of the 14 only restate the item name or its category, with no grape, region, style detail or ABV. 'Blanco tequila pour' under Blanco Tequila, 'VSOP Cognac pour' under Cognac VSOP, 'Hop-forward draft IPA' under Dry-Hopped IPA, 'Dry red wine' under Malbec and 'Dry sparkling cider' under Dry Cider all hit the criterion-12 'repeats the name' failure. Nothing on the page asks for the missing facts: no missing_ingredients flag is raised. Venue fit is also thin. For a Mexican cantina in Iowa City the list is one Margarita next to a Manhattan, a Daiquiri, a Czech Pilsner, a Malbec, a Pinot Grigio and a Cognac. The 'Agave' sub head holds only tequila, and apart from 'Añejo' there is no Spanish anywhere. The wordmark, the sun and the greca carry the whole Mexican identity, and the list does not back them up. Smaller points: (a) The Margarita alone mixes a middot ingredient list with the prose sentence 'Bright and citrus-forward.' (a draft sentence), so the menu speaks in two voices. (b) The Brown Butter Old Fashioned has public_visibility.house_recipe=false, yet the menu prints its full component list, 'aromatic bitters' included. That is allowed only if 'names only' is the confirmed rule for house_recipe=false; confirm it. (c) 'Cognac VSOP 18' can still read as an 18-year age statement, even with the lighter price weight. (d) Brut Rosé sits under 'Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label, so the guest cannot tell the pour. (e) The Old Fashioned description wraps to leave a stub second line, 'bitters · orange peel'. Price association passes: every price sits inline, 15.8 px after its name (1.9% of page width, per layout.json eye_travel), and no price is detached or ambiguous. Taglines pass: the only sub-line, '& cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa', states no item fact. The draft has 14 items and all 14 are printed. Junmai Ginjo is in phg.menu_items (price 12) but not in the draft doc; that is for the Content reviewer to confirm.
fixes: Replace the name-echo descriptions with sourced facts (grape and region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé; style and ABV for the three beers and the cider; age or category facts for the spirits), and raise missing_ingredients to the Coordinator for any fact phg.menu_items, brands, products or spirit_lexicon cannot supply, rather than printing 'X pour'.

Give the Margarita one voice: either drop 'Bright and citrus-forward.' or give every cocktail a short sensory line built from its recipe_versions row (rationale or method), so all four cocktails read alike.

Strengthen venue fit using only sourced content: rename the 'Agave' sub head 'Tequila', since only tequila is listed, and ask the Coordinator for the venue's Mexican beers, mezcal or house agave cocktails before the menu is final, because as sourced the list could belong to any American bar.

Label the pours (for example 'glass' next to Brut Rosé, and a pour size for the spirits if the draft supplies one), and rebalance the break in the Old Fashioned description so its second line is not a two-item stub (send this to the designer as a layout note).

Confirm with the Coordinator that house_recipe=false permits printing all component names for the Brown Butter Old Fashioned (7095fd3d); if it does not, cut the line back to the draft's 'Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.' and keep the orange peel garnish.
